sn7.13:1.2: _Vātehābādhika_ is a syntactic compound, “afflicted by winds” (_vātehi_). It is one of the illnesses noted at [an10.60:7.4](). In Ayurveda, diseases of the winds may have many causes, chief among them faulty digestion. Typically ghee or other oil is recommended rather than hot water.
sn7.13:1.3: In [dn16:5.4.5]() Upavāna was said to have been the Buddha’s carare for a long time. The events of this discourse are recalled by him in his verses at [thag2.33]().
